context:
Goal: one uniform direction for every watch, wake and hook (your item 180).
Problem (rule): you asked for an Opus check first. It found that all six must stay command hooks today. A built-in prompt hook gets only the tool input, has no fail-closed path and no effort setting, and your typed override cannot lift its deny.
Based on (measured): Opus audit, main 111b566b, read against code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, 08:43 CST Nov 5. call_judge: needs past rulings, the override lift and a fail-closed path. prose_judge: no override lift, no effort field; the nearest to a whole move. reply_judge: a Stop prompt hook forces the turn on; it cannot add a note. feedback_guard: reads and rewrites the inbox. report_guard: needs ruling records and a fail-closed path. sendmessage_state: its wording judge could split out once a prompt deny can be lifted.
Based on (read): whether a prompt hook runs on the session's sign-in or a token is unknown; the docs do not say.
Departs from: main (six callers start their own claude -p, no cost stated) — b adds each caller's cost and the re-run triggers to invoke_model's record; c adds a week of fire counts.

Re-run triggers: Claude Code adds an effort field, a fail-closed setting for prompt hooks, or a way to lift a prompt hook's deny.

options.gain: Nothing gets weaker; you see each hook's cost; a Claude Code change re-opens the move.
options.how: A lane writes each caller's cost (starts, time, token) and the three re-run triggers into invoke_model's record.
options.label: Keep all six, state each one's cost, and re-check on the triggers
options.lose: Each call still starts its own claude -p with your token.

options.gain: Hooks that never fire go away, with their token use.
options.how: A lane counts fires on demand from existing logs for a week, then brings a delete list.
options.label: Measure how often each fires for a week, then delete the ones that never fire
options.lose: A week before any change; a rare-but-real hook may look idle.

options.gain: No separate claude -p or token for moved hooks.
options.how: Not buildable as asked today: the audit found no hook whose event allows it without loss.
options.label: Move them to built-in prompt hooks anyway
options.lose: Fail-closed checks become fail-open, and your override can no longer lift those judges.

ref: item 180; step watcher-builtin-hook-survey; Opus audit 08:43 CST Nov 5 (coordinator)
title: None of the six model-call hooks can move to a built-in prompt hook today. What now?
why: Recommended: b. The audit found no safe move today, and b keeps every check while it records the cost and the triggers that re-open the move.
